claim: The extensive crosstalk between the developing heart and lung is critical to their proper morphogenesis and maturation.
source: The extensive crosstalk between the developing heart and lung is critical to their proper morphogenesis and maturation.
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research (Peng et al., 2013; Hoffmann et al., 2009; Arora et al., 2012; Steimle, 2018) in the Introduction section.

claim: During mouse embryonic development, WNT derived from the second heart field induces specification of pulmonary endoderm.
source: During mouse embryonic development, WNT derived from the second heart field induces specification of pulmonary endoderm, which in turn secretes SHH that signals back to the heart and regulates proper atrial septation (Steimle, 2018; Zhou, 2017; Hoffmann et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research (Steimle, 2018; Zhou, 2017; Hoffmann et al., 2009).

claim: Pulmonary endoderm secretes SHH that signals back to the heart and regulates proper atrial septation.
source: During mouse embryonic development, WNT derived from the second heart field induces specification of pulmonary endoderm, which in turn secretes SHH that signals back to the heart and regulates proper atrial septation (Steimle, 2018; Zhou, 2017; Hoffmann et al., 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research (Steimle, 2018; Zhou, 2017; Hoffmann et al., 2009).

claim: Inter-lineage crosstalk between heart and lung is partly mediated by multipotent mesodermal progenitors located between the developing heart and lung.
source: This inter-lineage crosstalk is partly mediated by the multipotent mesodermal progenitors located between the developing heart and lung, which have the potential for lineage contribution to pulmonary endothelium, pulmonary smooth muscle and cardiomyocytes (Peng et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research (Peng et al., 2013).

claim: Multipotent mesodermal progenitors have the potential for lineage contribution to pulmonary endothelium, pulmonary smooth muscle and cardiomyocytes.
source: This inter-lineage crosstalk is partly mediated by the multipotent mesodermal progenitors located between the developing heart and lung, which have the potential for lineage contribution to pulmonary endothelium, pulmonary smooth muscle and cardiomyocytes (Peng et al., 2013).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research (Peng et al., 2013).

claim: A stepwise differentiation strategy was developed to enable simultaneous specification of cardiac and pulmonary lineages within a single culture of hiPSCs.
source: Building on existing protocols on cardiac (Lian et al., 2012; Mummery et al., 2012; Burridge et al., 2014; Lian et al., 2015; Lee et al., 2017; Kattman et al., 2011; Laflamme et al., 2007), and lung (Chen et al., 2017; Huang et al., 2013; Jacob et al., 2017; Dye et al., 2015; Gotoh et al., 2014; D'Amour et al., 2005; Green et al., 2011) differentiation from hiPSCs, a stepwise differentiation strategy was developed to enable simultaneous specification of both lineages within a single culture of hiPSCs.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study, supported by experimental data shown in Figures 1-3.

claim: Balanced mesodermal and endodermal induction was achieved via fine-tuning of WNT activation in the absence of insulin, activin A, and BMP4 supplementation.
source: Firstly, a balanced mesodermal and endodermal induction was achieved via fine-tuning of WNT activation in the absence of insulin, activin A, and BMP4 supplementation (Stage-1).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figure 1.

claim: Combined inhibition of WNT and TGF-β signaling initiated the specification of co-induced mesoderm and endoderm towards cardiac and pulmonary specification.
source: Then, a combined inhibition of WNT and TGF-β signaling initiated the specification of the co-induced mesoderm and endoderm towards cardiac and pulmonary specification, respectively (Stage-2).
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figures 2-3.

claim: Reactivation of WNT signaling in the presence of retinoic acid led to concurrent emergence of NKX2.5+ cardiac and NKX2.1+ lung progenitors.
source: Lastly, reactivation of WNT signaling in the presence of retinoic acid (RA) led to concurrent emergence of NKX2.5+ cardiac and NKX2.1+ lung progenitors (Stage-3), which was our main focus in this study.
evidence: This is a primary finding supported by experimental data in Figure 2.

claim: 7 μM CHIR drives balanced endoderm and mesoderm induction from hiPSCs.
source: This observation was further confirmed by gene expression analysis of FOXA2, SOX17, and NCAM1 (Figure 1d), which together suggests that 7 μM CHIR drives balanced endoderm and mesoderm induction from hiPSCs, while further elevation of CHIR dosage selectively favors mesodermal specification.
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1d and immunofluorescence data in Figure 1b-c.

claim: Further elevation of CHIR dosage above 7 μM selectively favors mesodermal specification.
source: This observation was further confirmed by gene expression analysis of FOXA2, SOX17, and NCAM1 (Figure 1d), which together suggests that 7 μM CHIR drives balanced endoderm and mesoderm induction from hiPSCs, while further elevation of CHIR dosage selectively favors mesodermal specification.
evidence: Supported by gene expression data shown in Figure 1d.

claim: Upon 48 hr induction with 7 μM CHIR, the majority of cells were expressing primitive streak marker (T) and mesendoderm marker (MIXL1), but not pluripotent marker (OCT4).
source: We confirmed that upon 48 hr induction with 7 μM CHIR, the majority of cells were expressing primitive streak marker (T) and mesendoderm marker (MIXL1), but not pluripotent marker (OCT4) during early germ layer induction (Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: WNT induces formation of primitive streak after 48 hr of treatment.
source: This is in line with a study by Martyn et al., 2019 demonstrating that WNT induces formation of primitive streak after 48 hr of treatment and that the newly formed primitive streak cells provide additional endogenous WNT, BMP, and Nodal signaling to further pattern the cells toward mesoderm and endoderm lineage (Martyn et al., 2019),
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research (Martyn et al., 2019).

claim: Newly formed primitive streak cells provide additional endogenous WNT, BMP, and Nodal signaling to further pattern the cells toward mesoderm and endoderm lineage.
source: This is in line with a study by Martyn et al., 2019 demonstrating that WNT induces formation of primitive streak after 48 hr of treatment and that the newly formed primitive streak cells provide additional endogenous WNT, BMP, and Nodal signaling to further pattern the cells toward mesoderm and endoderm lineage (Martyn et al., 2019),
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research (Martyn et al., 2019).

claim: Cells pre-exposed to CHIR (7 μM) during Stage-1 were able to give rise to robust co-induction of both cardiac (NKX2.5+) and pulmonary (NKX2.1+) progenitors on Day-15.
source: We found that on Day-15, cells pre-exposed to CHIR (7 μM) during Stage-1 were able to give rise to robust co-induction of both cardiac (NKX2.5+) and pulmonary (NKX2.1+) progenitors (Figure 2c, d and e).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 2c-e.

claim: Cells pre-treated with high-CHIR (10 μM) differentiated mainly into cardiac lineage.
source: In comparison, cells pre-treated with high-CHIR (10 μM) differentiated mainly into cardiac lineage; while low-CHIR (4 μM) failed to drive effective differentiation into either lineage (Figure 2c, d and e).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 2c-e.

claim: Low-CHIR (4 μM) failed to drive effective differentiation into either cardiac or pulmonary lineage.
source: In comparison, cells pre-treated with high-CHIR (10 μM) differentiated mainly into cardiac lineage; while low-CHIR (4 μM) failed to drive effective differentiation into either lineage (Figure 2c, d and e).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 2c-e.

claim: NKX2.1+ cells did not co-express TUJ1/PAX6 (Neural) or PAX8 (Thyroid), suggesting that the specified NKX2.1+ population is of lung fate.
source: Our results showed the NKX2.1+ cells did not co-express TUJ1/PAX6 (Neural) or PAX8 (Thyroid), suggesting that the specified NKX2.1+ population is of lung fate.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d.

claim: No p63-expressing cells were identified on Day-15, confirming the absence of airway epithelial cell population.
source: Furthermore, no p63-expressing cells were identified, confirming the absence of airway epithelial cell population.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d.

claim: NKX2.5+ cells co-expressed cardiac Troponin T (cTnT), suggesting that these cells were being specified towards cardiac lineage.
source: At the same stage, NKX2.5+ cells co-expressed cardiac Troponin T (cTnT), suggesting that these cells were being specified towards cardiac lineage.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d.

claim: COUPTFII-positive staining was observed in some of the NKX2.5+ cells, suggesting atrial specification.
source: COUPTFII-positive staining was also observed in some of the NKX2.5+ cells, suggesting atrial specification.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d.

claim: Most of the NKX2.5+ cells on Day-15 have yet to specify into downstream cardiac subtypes such as ventricular (MLC2v), endocardium (NFATC), and epicardium (WT1).
source: However, most of the NKX2.5+ cells have yet to specific into downstream cardiac subtypes such as ventricular (MLC2v), endocardium (NFATC), and epicardium (WT1) (Figure 2—figure supplement 1d).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1d.

claim: Extended CHIR exposure for 48 or 72 hr was required to induce robust cardio-pulmonary programs.
source: We evaluated the efficiency of cardio-pulmonary induction following exposure to CHIR (7 µM) for different periods (24, 48, and 72 hr), and found that extended CHIR exposure for 48 or 72 hr was required to induce robust cardio-pulmonary programs (Figure 2f).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2f-h.

claim: CHIR favored cardiac specification with increase in exposure time and plateaued at 48 hr of treatment.
source: Specifically, CHIR favored cardiac specification with increase in exposure time and plateaued at 48 hr of treatment (Figure 2h);
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2h.

claim: The induction of pulmonary program peaked at 48 hr of CHIR treatment and declined with further extension of the treatment.
source: while the induction of pulmonary program peaked at 48 hr of CHIR treatment (Figure 2g) and declined with further extension of the treatment.
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 2g.

claim: Maintaining hiPSCs in mTESR1 Plus during the initial CHIR treatment appeared to be critical for enabling effective cardio-pulmonary differentiation.
source: Furthermore, we showed that maintaining hiPSCs in mTESR1 Plus during the initial CHIR treatment appeared to be critical for enabling effective cardio-pulmonary differentiation (Figure 3—figure supplement 1), as compared to using RPMI1640 supplemented with B-27 minus insulin as the basal medium during CHIR treatment.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: Nodal signaling inhibition (using A8301, Day-2 to Day-4) immediately following CHIR treatment terminated both cardiac and pulmonary induction.
source: Nodal signaling inhibition (using A8301, Day-2 to Day-4) immediately following CHIR treatment terminated both cardiac and pulmonary induction; while nodal activation through Activin A supplementation (Day-2 to Day-4) led to pulmonary-only differentiation (Figure 3a, b and c).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 3a-c.

claim: Nodal activation through Activin A supplementation (Day-2 to Day-4) led to pulmonary-only differentiation.
source: Nodal signaling inhibition (using A8301, Day-2 to Day-4) immediately following CHIR treatment terminated both cardiac and pulmonary induction; while nodal activation through Activin A supplementation (Day-2 to Day-4) led to pulmonary-only differentiation (Figure 3a, b and c).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 3a-c.

claim: Endogenous nodal signaling is required for cardio-pulmonary induction.
source: This suggests the requirement of endogenous nodal signaling for cardio-pulmonary induction and that high-level nodal activation favors pulmonary instead of cardiac induction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that nodal inhibition terminates both cardiac and pulmonary induction.

claim: High-level nodal activation favors pulmonary instead of cardiac induction.
source: This suggests the requirement of endogenous nodal signaling for cardio-pulmonary induction and that high-level nodal activation favors pulmonary instead of cardiac induction.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that Activin A supplementation leads to pulmonary-only differentiation.

claim: BMP inhibition (using DMH-1) during Day-2 to Day-4 compromised cardiac induction and mildly reduced pulmonary specification.
source: In parallel, BMP inhibition (using DMH-1) during the same time period compromised cardiac induction and mildly reduced pulmonary specification; while exogenous BMP4 supplementation enhanced cardiac induction but inhibited pulmonary specification (Figure 3d, e and f).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 3d-f.

claim: Exogenous BMP4 supplementation enhanced cardiac induction but inhibited pulmonary specification.
source: In parallel, BMP inhibition (using DMH-1) during the same time period compromised cardiac induction and mildly reduced pulmonary specification; while exogenous BMP4 supplementation enhanced cardiac induction but inhibited pulmonary specification (Figure 3d, e and f).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 3d-f.

claim: Endogenous BMP signaling is primarily required for cardiac induction.
source: This indicates that endogenous BMP signaling is primarily required for cardiac induction and that exogenous augmentation of BMP signaling further favors the cardiac lineage at the expense of the pulmonary lineage.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that BMP inhibition compromises cardiac induction.

claim: Exogenous augmentation of BMP signaling further favors the cardiac lineage at the expense of the pulmonary lineage.
source: This indicates that endogenous BMP signaling is primarily required for cardiac induction and that exogenous augmentation of BMP signaling further favors the cardiac lineage at the expense of the pulmonary lineage.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that BMP4 supplementation enhances cardiac induction but inhibits pulmonary specification.

claim: Combined TGF-β and WNT inhibition enhanced both cardiac and pulmonary specification.
source: We found that combined TGF-β and WNT inhibition enhanced both cardiac and pulmonary specification, with TGF-β inhibition having a more profound effect on the cardiac lineage (Figure 3—figure supplement 2b,c,d).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2b-d.

claim: TGF-β inhibition has a more profound effect on cardiac lineage specification than WNT inhibition.
source: We found that combined TGF-β and WNT inhibition enhanced both cardiac and pulmonary specification, with TGF-β inhibition having a more profound effect on the cardiac lineage (Figure 3—figure supplement 2b,c,d).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 2b-d.

claim: There was no significant differences observed at protein and gene expression level of NKX2.1 and NKX2.5 comparing ventralization in the presence and absence of exogenous BMP4.
source: Intriguingly, there was no significant differences observed at protein and gene expression level of NKX2.1 and NKX2.5 comparing ventralization in the presence and absence of exogenous BMP4 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3b,c,d).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3b-d.

claim: Endogenous BMP4 was required during ventralization stage of differentiation.
source: Nonetheless, endogenous BMP4 was indeed required during this stage of differentiation, as inhibition of BMP4 using DMH1 significantly compromised the induction of both NKX2.1 and NKX2.5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3b,c,d).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3b-d.

claim: Inhibition of BMP4 using DMH1 significantly compromised the induction of both NKX2.1 and NKX2.5.
source: Nonetheless, endogenous BMP4 was indeed required during this stage of differentiation, as inhibition of BMP4 using DMH1 significantly compromised the induction of both NKX2.1 and NKX2.5 (Figure 3—figure supplement 3b,c,d).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence and qPCR data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 3b-d.

claim: Upon transition from 2D to 3D suspension culture in CKDCI medium, the co-induced cardio-pulmonary progenitors self-assembled into pulmonary-centered, concentric, dual-lineage μTs during the overnight culture.
source: Upon transition from 2D to 3D suspension culture in CKDCI medium, the co-induced cardio-pulmonary progenitors self-assembled into pulmonary-centered, concentric, dual-lineage μTs during the overnight culture (Figure 4b).
evidence: Supported by whole mount staining shown in Figure 4b.

claim: Following 3 days of 3D suspension culture in CKDCI medium, effective AT2 maturation was observed in the cardio-pulmonary μTs.
source: Following 3 days of 3D suspension culture in CKDCI medium, effective AT2 maturation was observed in the cardio-pulmonary μTs as indicated by robust SFTPCTdTomato fluorescence (Figure 4c) and gene expression (Figure 4—figure supplement 1c).
evidence: Supported by fluorescence imaging in Figure 4c and qPCR data in Figure 4—figure supplement 1c.

claim: The SFTPCTdTomato fluorescence could sustained up to Day-29 (2 weeks in alveolar maturation medium).
source: The SFTPCTdTomato fluorescence could sustained up to Day-29 (2 weeks in alveolar maturation medium) (Figure 4—figure supplement 1a,b).
evidence: Supported by fluorescence imaging shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1a-b.

claim: Day-15 cardio-pulmonary progenitors cultured on transwell insert for air-liquid interface (ALI) culture failed to detect obvious AT2 induction by Day-18.
source: As a control, we cultured Day-15 cardio-pulmonary progenitors on top of the transwell insert for air-liquid interface (ALI) culture, on 2D plastic surface for regular submerged culture or embedded in Growth Factor Reduced (GFR) Matrigel, and failed to detect obvious AT2 induction by Day-18 (Figure 4c, Figure 4—figure supplement 2, Figure 4—figure supplement 3).
evidence: Supported by fluorescence imaging shown in Figure 4c and supplementary figures.

claim: NKX2.1 and SFTPC gene expression was significantly upregulated in 3D suspension culture on Day-18 compared to the starting Day-15 cells or cells following ALI maturation.
source: Consistent with the observations using fluorescence reporters, NKX2.1 and SFTPC gene expression was significantly upregulated in 3D suspension culture on Day-18 compared to the starting Day-15 cells or cells following ALI maturation (Figure 4d and e).
evidence: Supported by qPCR data shown in Figure 4d-e.

claim: 3D suspension culture is a robust platform to expedite alveolar maturation.
source: Our results demonstrated 3D suspension culture as a robust platform to expedite alveolar maturation.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the experimental data showing effective AT2 maturation in 3D suspension culture compared to other culture methods.

claim: In the absence of accompanying cardiac cells, NKX2.1GFP+ lung progenitors could not achieve as effective AT2 maturation as what is observed in cardio-pulmonary μTs.
source: In the absence of accompanying cardiac cells, although NKX2.1GFP+ lung progenitors can be robustly induced and maintained, their alveolar maturation (as indicated by SFTPCtdTomato reporter) following 3 days of maturation in 3D suspension culture was dramatically diminished compared to the cardio-pulmonary group (Figure 4g–l).
evidence: Supported by fluorescence imaging and qPCR data shown in Figure 4g-n.

claim: Cardio-pulmonary μTs possessed a concentric arrangement of NKX2.1+ cells, surrounded by NKX2.5+ cells on Day-18.
source: Whole mount imaging of μTs on Day-18 showed pulmonary-only differentiation mainly comprised NKX2.1+ cells, while cardio-pulmonary μTs possessed a concentric arrangement of NKX2.1+ cells, surrounded by NKX2.5+ cells (Figure 4i and j).
evidence: Supported by whole mount staining shown in Figure 4i-j.

claim: The cardiac lineage can serve as a cellular niche in supporting alveolar maturation.
source: This suggests that the cardiac lineage can serve as a cellular niche in supporting alveolar maturation.
evidence: This is an inference based on the experimental data showing that alveolar maturation is diminished in the absence of cardiac cells.

claim: The cardio-pulmonary co-induction protocol is reproducible using another independent hiPSC line (BU1).
source: We confirmed the reproducibility of our cardio-pulmonary co-induction protocol using another independent hiPSC line (BU1), including effective induction of endodermal and mesodermal mixture on Day-4 (Figure 4—figure supplement 5a,b), induction of pulmonary (NKX2.1) and cardiac (NKX2.5) progenitors on Day-15 (Figure 4—figure supplement 5c,d), and maturation of alveolar type two epithelium (Pro-SFTPC), and cardiac structural markers (cTnT and Sarcomeric Alpha Actinin) on Day-18 μTs (Figure 4—figure supplement 5e).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 5.

claim: Upon CHIR removal, the cardiac and pulmonary components within each dual-lineage μT effectively reorganized over time and eventually segregated from each other.
source: To our surprise, upon CHIR removal, the cardiac and pulmonary components within each dual-lineage μT, which was initially arranged in the pulmonary-centered, concentric manner (Figure 5b), effectively reorganized over time and eventually segregated from each other (Figure 5a and b).
evidence: Supported by histological analysis shown in Figure 5a-b and time-lapse imaging.

claim: Cardio-pulmonary segregation took place in both CKDCI and KDCI medium conditions, but was significantly expedited by the withdrawal of CHIR.
source: We compared the segregation process in the presence (CKDCI) and absence (KDCI) of CHIR, and found that although cardio-pulmonary segregation took place in both medium conditions, it was significantly expedited by the withdrawal of CHIR (Figure 5d,).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Inhibition of canonical (IWP4) and non-canonical (NSC668036) WNT signaling did not obviously affect the segregation process.
source: To investigate the requirement of endogenous WNT signaling for this segregation process, we introduced inhibitors of canonical (IWP4) and non-canonical (NSC668036, a Dishevelled inhibitor) WNT signaling (Li and Wang, 2018), and did not detect any obvious difference in the segregation process as compared to the control KDCI condition (Figure 5d).
evidence: Supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 5d.

claim: Cardiac contraction was observed 7 days following CHIR withdrawal.
source: In parallel with the cardio-pulmonary segregation, cardiac contraction was observed 7 days following CHIR withdrawal (Video 1).
evidence: Supported by video evidence (Video 1).

claim: Lamellar bodies were detected in cardio-pulmonary μTs by transmission electron microscopy.
source: The induction of AT2 cells were further confirmed by the detection of the presence of lamellar bodies by transmission electron microscopy (Figure 6a)
evidence: Supported by TEM imaging shown in Figure 6a.

claim: Cardio-pulmonary μTs expressed pro-SFTPC+ and pro-SFTPB+ markers.
source: and by the positive immunofluorescence staining of pro-SFTPC+ (Figure 6b) and pro-SFTPB+ (Figure 6—figure supplement 1a).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6b and Figure 6—figure supplement 1a.

claim: HOPX+ cells were observed in the μTs, suggesting the presence of AT1-like cells.
source: We also observed HOPX+ cells in the μTs (Figure 6b), and upregulated HOPX gene expression (Figure 6—figure supplement 1b) suggesting the presence of AT1-like cells.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data in Figure 6b and qPCR data in Figure 6—figure supplement 1b.

claim: S100A4 staining indicated presence of mesenchyme in the μTs.
source: S100A4 staining indicated presence of mesenchyme in the μTs (Figure 6—figure supplement 1c), which may also play an important role in promoting alveologenesis Hawkins et al., 2017.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1c.

claim: Cardio-pulmonary μTs did not express markers for proximal airway epithelium such as ciliated cells (FOXJ1), secretory cells (MUC5AC) and basal cells (p63).
source: In the meantime, these μTs did not express markers for proximal airway epithelium such as ciliated cells (FOXJ1) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1d), secretory cells (MUC5AC) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1e) and basal cells (p63) (Figure 6—figure supplement 1f), which can be readily observed in airway μT engineered from bronchial epithelial cells.
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6—figure supplement 1d-f.

claim: Cardiac elements within the μTs exhibited the striated pattern as indicated by cTnT and Sarcomeric Alpha Actinin staining.
source: In parallel, cardiac elements within the μTs exhibited the striated pattern as indicated by cTnT and Sarcomeric Alpha Actinin staining (Figure 6c and d).
evidence: Supported by immunofluorescence data shown in Figure 6c-d.

claim: Cardiac contractile function was confirmed via the detection of calcium influx.
source: The cardiac contractile function was confirmed via the detection of calcium influx (Video 2), and its gradual reduction with increasing concentrations of Verapamil, a calcium channel blocker (Figure 6e).
evidence: Supported by calcium imaging data shown in Video 2 and Figure 6e.

claim: Cardiac contractile function showed gradual reduction with increasing concentrations of Verapamil, a calcium channel blocker.
source: The cardiac contractile function was confirmed via the detection of calcium influx (Video 2), and its gradual reduction with increasing concentrations of Verapamil, a calcium channel blocker (Figure 6e).
evidence: Supported by calcium imaging data shown in Figure 6e.

claim: Both endodermal and mesodermal specification is facilitated by the inhibition of insulin and phosphoinositide 3-kinase signaling.
source: Firstly, both endodermal and mesodermal specification is facilitated by the inhibition of insulin and phosphoinositide 3-kinase signaling (Lian et al., 2012; Lian et al., 2013; Mou et al., 2012), and can be induced by a similar set of paracrine factors, including WNT, BMP, and TGF-β (Kattman et al., 2011; D'Amour et al., 2005; Loh, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Endodermal and mesodermal specification can be induced by a similar set of paracrine factors, including WNT, BMP, and TGF-β.
source: Firstly, both endodermal and mesodermal specification is facilitated by the inhibition of insulin and phosphoinositide 3-kinase signaling (Lian et al., 2012; Lian et al., 2013; Mou et al., 2012), and can be induced by a similar set of paracrine factors, including WNT, BMP, and TGF-β (Kattman et al., 2011; D'Amour et al., 2005; Loh, 2014).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The quantitative combination of WNT, BMP, and TGF-β signaling determines endoderm versus mesoderm bifurcation.
source: It is the quantitative combination of these signaling that determines endoderm versus mesoderm bifurcation (Kattman et al., 2011; Loh, 2014; Kim, 2015).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Endoderm and mesoderm share primitive streak origin during gastrulation.
source: This is consistent with the shared primitive streak origin of both germ layers during gastrulation (Levak-Svajger and Svajger, 1974; Lawson et al., 1991; Tam and Beddington, 1987).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research.

claim: WNT inhibition facilitates the transition from definitive endoderm to anterior foregut endoderm.
source: Secondly, WNT inhibition not only facilitates the transition from definitive endoderm to anterior foregut endoderm (Loh, 2014; Spence et al., 2011), but it also promotes cardiac mesoderm emergence (Lian et al., 2012; Willems et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011; Ren et al., 2011; Tran, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research.

claim: WNT inhibition promotes cardiac mesoderm emergence.
source: Secondly, WNT inhibition not only facilitates the transition from definitive endoderm to anterior foregut endoderm (Loh, 2014; Spence et al., 2011), but it also promotes cardiac mesoderm emergence (Lian et al., 2012; Willems et al., 2011; Wang et al., 2011; Ren et al., 2011; Tran, 2009).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Retinoic acid (RA) signaling is required for the induction and maturation of both cardiac and pulmonary progenitors.
source: Lastly, retinoic acid (RA) signaling is required for the induction and maturation of both cardiac and pulmonary progenitors (Huang et al., 2013; Jacob et al., 2017; Mou et al., 2012; Chen, 2007; McCauley et al., 2017).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Common paracrine regulation of paralleled cardiac and pulmonary specification is consistent with their close spatial coordinates within the embryonic body planning.
source: These common paracrine regulation of paralleled cardiac and pulmonary specification is consistent with their close spatial coordinates within the embryonic body planning, as demonstrated by shared HOX genes expression and functional requirement (Lufkin et al., 1991; Makki and Capecchi, 2012; Chisaka and Capecchi, 1991).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Cardiac and pulmonary development share HOX genes expression and functional requirement.
source: These common paracrine regulation of paralleled cardiac and pulmonary specification is consistent with their close spatial coordinates within the embryonic body planning, as demonstrated by shared HOX genes expression and functional requirement (Lufkin et al., 1991; Makki and Capecchi, 2012; Chisaka and Capecchi, 1991).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research.

claim: Continuous exposure to WNT activation is known to delay contractile maturation of cardiomyocytes.
source: Spatial-temporal regulation of WNT is crucial for early cardiac differentiation (Lian et al., 2012; Zhao et al., 2019; Buikema et al., 2020), however, continuous exposure to WNT activation is known to delay contractile maturation of cardiomyocytes (Fan et al., 2018).
evidence: Supported by citation to prior research (Fan et al., 2018).

claim: Exogenous WNT activation using CHIR is essential for inducing AT2 maturation and its maintenance until the endogenous AT2 niche is established.
source: In parallel, exogenous WNT activation using CHIR is essential for inducing AT2 maturation and its maintenance until the endogenous AT2 niche is established (Jacob et al., 2017; Abdelwahab et al., 2019; Nabhan et al., 2018; Frank et al., 2016).
evidence: Supported by citations to prior research.

claim: The multilineage differentiation model offers an experimentally tractable system for investigating human cardio-pulmonary interaction and tissue boundary formation during embryogenesis.
source: We expect that our multilineage differentiation model will offer an experimentally tractable system for investigating human cardio-pulmonary interaction and tissue boundary formation during embryogenesis.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential applications of the model.

claim: The model could be useful for studying congenital diseases affecting both cardiovascular and pulmonary systems, such as congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
source: We also expect this work to be of potential use for studying congenital diseases affecting both cardiovascular and pulmonary systems, such as congenital diaphragmatic hernia.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about the potential applications of the model.
